facts.text: Goodman was renamed after Lowell Goodman, a pioneer orchardist who founded the Ozark Orchard Company and helped shape the town’s early economy.
Before settlers arrived, the area that is now Goodman lay within the Osage Nation’s territory until the Osage were forcibly removed by the U.S. government.
The Kansas City, Pittsburg and Gulf Railroad’s arrival in the late 1890s turned the small siding known as Donahue into the first railroad town in McDonald County.
Goodman sits on a ridge that drains east to Indian Creek, south to Beaver Branch, and west to the Sugar Fork of Buffalo Creek.
The entire town lies within the Elk River watershed, a major tributary of the Neosho River, where karst groundwater flow shapes seasonal streams.
